answer: In an attestation graph G, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so voting weight depends on reachable, independently endorsed paths rather than identity count. A sybil cluster S with few external attestations has a small cut and low conductance, Φ(S)=cut(S,V\S)/vol(S), limiting walk flow into it. Given capped seed mass and walk length, min-cut and transitivity bounds constrain its aggregate voting weight, even when pearl, fable, and saffron are labels inside the cluster.
